To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prolonged preincubational egg storage (2 3 weeks at room temperature) impairs viability, size and physiological function in chicken embryos.

prolonged preincubational egg storage (2 3 weeks) at room temperature (22 degrees C) impairs viability, size, and physiological functions of chicken embryos, but storage for 1 3 weeks at 15 degrees C has a more severe effect on viability, but less severe effect on embryo size and physiological functions compared with room temperature storage.

preincubated chicken eggs stored at 22deg C for 3 weeks had reduced embryo viability, whereas eggs stored at 1 5deg C for 2 weeks resulted in decreased embryo size and altered physiological functions (Hct, [Rbc], and [Hb]) in embryos.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of preincubation temperature on the development of embryos in chicken eggs, and the consequences of such developmental programming for physiological function and performance in the adult animal.
the developmental programming effects of preincubation conditions on the physiology of chicken embryos.
understanding the mechanisms by which the developing chicken blastodisc is able to maintain viability during prolonged preincubatory storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

preincubating chicken eggs at a cooler temperature (15degC) than normal (22degC) for 2 weeks results in reduced embryo size and impaired viability, but better regulation of acid base and blood gas status than preincubation at 22deg C.
prolonged storage of avian eggs at 15 or 22degC, especially at the lower temperature, results in embryonic programming that alters viability, size, and physiological functions of day 15 embryos.

preincubated eggs stored at 22deg C for 1 3 weeks resulted in poor viability, reduced body mass and impaired regulation of physiological functions in day 16 chicken embryos compared with embryos from eggs stored at 1 5degC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
preincubational storage at room temperature (22 deg C) resulted in poor viability and reduced body size compared to storage at 15 deg C, but physiological function was better.
preincubated eggs are a useful model to study the effects of altered preincubication conditions on the developing embryo.
preincubated egg storage in the cold is a useful model for investigating the effects of embryonic programming on the physiology of the embryo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the preincubation temperature and duration of egg storage can have profound effects on the viability, body mass and physiology of developing embryos, and these changes can be detected even after only 1 week of egg storage.
preincubational storage conditions (duration, temperature and gaseous environment) can affect embryo viability, size, and physiological functions.
embryonic programming is a real phenomenon in avian eggs, but the effects of preincubation temperature are not always predictable and can be dependent on the duration of storage.
